questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: You can take any course you want for the first couple of weeks. The courses I ended up taking were more practical and hands-on which I really enjoyed.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Before going I knew that Geneva was expensive, but I was still surprised by the price level.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Alcohol was fairly cheap, but everything else was more expensive than back home. Eating out, grocery shopping and such

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Many clubs and initiatives

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Running club, basketball, investing club and such.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Join the Erasmus trips. A good way to go somewhere for cheap with some nice people

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go out in the nature, travel by train. Go to Bains des Pâquis for sauna, dip and drinks.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Quite easy, It's quite an international city. However, not speaking french was sometimes a bit of an issue.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Join the clubs. Try to be a bit more outgoing than you usually would. The Swiss are quite reserved like the Danes, but are quite nice once they open up.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The difference in class/economic background was very diverse. Back home everyone has kind of the same point of reference. However, in Geneva it felt like there was a team A and team B.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Relatively punctual, takes accountability.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Find housing fast through the institution, Go to France for bigger grocery shopping trips, money are temporary, memories are forever :)

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Public transport is free for students under the age of 25 I believe.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Seeing so much incredible nature and having great lectures.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Justifying spending a large amount of money on travelling and going out in general.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
